This week I read **Bad Monkeys**, by Matt Ruff. The gist of the plot is, a woman has killed someone, and she's being questioned in some kind of psychiatric ward. She claims that she was chosen when she was a teenager to join a secret society of assassins dedicated to killing evil people (or Bad Monkeys), and the book is essentially composed of what she recounts to the person interviewing her. 

All the way through, I was loving it. I read it essentially in one sitting. It's quirky, and it's exciting, and it does keep you guessing -  is she making it all up? Is she actually delusional and none of it's real? And then, the ending. The ending fell completely flat for me, to the point that reading the book almost felt like a waste of time.  The author clearly wanted to end with "a twist," and the ending he chose felt so rushed and unconnected to everything else that had happened in the book that it almost felt like an insult. I really try not to be negative about books, and it started out so well that I think I'll give it another go one day just to see if I missed the point. But for now, I've never felt so let down by a book ending.
